title: The Slippery Slope Blocker
subtitle: What does "use strict" actually forbid?
description: Strict mode turns several silent failures into errors.
prompt:
Which behaviour is changed by strict mode?

**A.** Array indices become 1-based
**B.** All asynchronous code becomes synchronous
**C.** Assigning to an undeclared variable throws a ReferenceError
**D.** Loose equality (==) is disabled at parse time
options: Assigning to an undeclared variable throws a ReferenceError
Loose equality (==) is disabled at parse time
hints: Modules are always strict — how often do you see the directive there?

solution.summary: The correct answer is C — Assigning to an undeclared variable throws a ReferenceError
solution.answer: Assigning to an undeclared variable throws a ReferenceError
reasoning: Strict mode’s headline fixes: no implicit globals, this is undefined in bare calls, duplicate parameter names rejected, silent write failures throw.
It is opt-in per script/module/function via the "use strict" directive; ES modules are always strict.
whyNot: Array indices become 1-based — Indexing is unchanged everywhere — strict mode has nothing to do with arrays’ indexing.
All asynchronous code becomes synchronous — Strict mode changes error reporting and bindings, never the concurrency model.
Loose equality (==) is disabled at parse time — == keeps working; linters discourage it, but the language does not forbid it.

learningObjectives: Know where strict mode applies automatically
